newsitem.title: ROMANIA: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 4 PM.
newsitem.headline: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 4 PM.

text.p: * President Ion Iliescu met representatives of major trade unions countrywide to answer questions on his commitment to reform and improving living standards.

He said he was willing to support the government formed by the Democratic Convention (CDR) and the Social Democratic Union (USD) provided that their platform would fulfil their electoral promises and not stir social unrest.
Iliescu said the president should not have the same political affiliation as the ruling coalition in order to preserve national stability.
* Democratic Convention (CDR) leader Emil Constantinescu outlined the first steps to be taken by the new government and CDR strategy to win Sunday's run-off in presidential polls.
* Constantinescu said no agreement was signed with the Hungarian Democratic Union, which won about six percent of the vote in parliamentary elections.
* The CDR executive discussed Iliescu's latest statements during the campaign in Braila and Alba Iulia.
* The national radio will hold two separate talk shows for the two contenders in this week's run-off presidential election.
The two are to answer questions from the radio audience.

* The November 3 general and presidential polls were fraught with irregularities, the leader of the human rights group LADO said. He quoted numerous infractions, including erroneous electoral lists. ($= 3,450 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
